A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OptFPRL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: Appendix F and Figure 2 report original numerical experiments comparing OptFPRL, FTRL, and OMD across six synthetic nonstationary scenarios.

after.justification: Appendix F and Figure 2 retain the original numerical experiments and their reported outcomes across six synthetic nonstationary scenarios.

M1.justification: The update, pruning rule, and four regularization strategies are unchanged. Algorithm 1 now explicitly says to omit the indicator function; that unconstrained computation was already specified in v1's Section 3 and Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six synthetic linear-loss OCO scenarios, covering changes in cost direction, switching frequency, magnitude, and prediction quality. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Appendix F retains FTRL with adaptive Euclidean regularization and OMD with adaptive learning rates as comparators, including their optimistic forms in Scenario 6. Comparator participation is unchanged.

E3.justification: The experimental domain, declared horizon, cost schedules, tuning, and prediction construction are unchanged. Figure 2(f)'s revised average-regret label matches the caption and prose already present in v1, supporting a labeling correction rather than a protocol change.

E4.justification: The switching-frequency and magnitude comparisons, prediction-quality example, and Scenario 5 failure case are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analytical experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 2's dashed overlays retain their stated role of identifying iterate–comparator mismatches.

E6.justification: Figure 2 retains the same plotted trajectories and reported findings, including OptFPRL's worse performance in Scenario 5. The Scenario 6 axis relabeling does not introduce new numerical outcomes.

T1.justification: Settings 1 corrects H_T's summation endpoint from T to T−1. The Lemma 4.2 proof corrects r_{t+1} to r_t, while Lemma D.3 changes its upper bound from a square root of summed a_t to summed a_t squared and changes one proof inequality to equality. These are localized mathematical revisions; the principal theorem bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: pruning enables optimistic dynamic-regret guarantees for FTRL, prediction accuracy modulates the bounds, and recursive regularization provides finer control.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a conditional interpretation of consistent pruning as permitting equivalence to one-step optimistic mirror descent through Ada-MD's flexible q_t terms. Existing explanations of tuning effects, excessive agility, and the Scenario 5 failure remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed regularization formulas, numerical setup, prediction construction, and code-access reference are retained. The Algorithm 1 clarification repeats information already available in v1 rather than supplying a new implementation detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang et al. (2016) to the prior-path-length discussion and explicitly connects pruning to Joulani et al. (2020) in Appendix A.3. Appendix E also changes Scroccaro et al. (2023)'s best-case summary under online path estimation from O(1+P_T) to O(P_T).

P1.justification: There are localized wording and notation edits, clearer Algorithm 1 wording, an additional explanatory paragraph in Appendix A.3, and an explicit Appendix heading. The overall section order and most prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains a (−1,0) direction annotation and an edited caption. Figure 2(f)'s axis changes from Regret R_T to Average Regret R_T/T while retaining its curves. Appendix additions cause limited page-break shifts without adding or removing figures.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves internal consistency through the H_T endpoint and regularizer-index corrections, clearer algorithm wording, and the corrected Figure 2(f) label. The added mirror-descent connection also clarifies positioning. These gains are limited: Lemma D.3 still has a denominator mismatch between statement and proof, and Appendix E's O(P_T) rewrite loses precision near P_T=0.
